item.title: Reinsurance inflection – Key question is whether irrational competition emerges: AM Best
item.description: With reinsurance capital across the market now at record levels , the rating agency says the key question is, “whether reinsurers can maintain underwriting discipline or will irrational competition emerge leading to another traditional soft market cycle.” Unlike previous hard market cycles, capital accumulated to incumbents rather than a wave of start-ups, as supportive market conditions continue to drive favourable earnings generation for reinsurers. “Consequently, maintaining pricing discipline in casualty business may ultimately prove as important as preserving discipline within the property catastrophe market.” AM Best highlighted the growing investor interest in casualty-linked structures in the insurance-linked securities marketplace, but noted that, “the attractiveness of property catastrophe ILS has proven difficult to replicate within casualty business.” Favourable earnings profile could persist for reinsurance players barring an outsized catastrophe event, but the most important question is whether reinsurers can maintain their pricing discipline, the rating agency said. The global reinsurance market is at an inflection point after consecutive strong year’s of underwriting returns have driven robust capital generation, while inflows continue to grow the insurance-linked securities market and alternative forms of capacity, which leads AM Best to call this an inflection point and ask if pricing discipline will last.

item.title: Strong July boosts UCITS catastrophe bond fund returns, but 12-month drops below 10%
item.description: Catastrophe bond fund strategies in the UCITS format saw performance accelerate through recent weeks as seasonality boosted returns, but the 12-month rolling return average across the Plenum CAT Bond UCITS Fund Indices has now declined to just under 10% for the first time this year. The average return of UCITS catastrophe bond funds for the period from the nearest last end of month reporting of this Index, on June 26th through to July 31st 2026, reached 1.15%. As a result, the average year-to-date performance of the UCITS catastrophe bond fund strategies rose from 2.91% at June 26th 2026, to now 4.09% as of July 31st.

item.title: Hiscox Capital Partners hires Spanos as Senior ILS Actuary
item.description: Hiscox Capital Partners, the division of Hiscox Re that encompasses insurance-linked securities (ILS) investments and quota-share partnerships, has appointed Charalambos (Harry) Spanos as a Senior ILS Actuary. Based in London, Spanos, a seasoned and qualified actuary, has joined Hiscox Capital Partners, bringing with him a decade of experience in ILS and reinsurance. Earlier this year, Hiscox Re, the reinsurance division of Hiscox Group launched Hiscox Capital Partners as a new business unit to consolidate all the capital partnership activity the organisation has managed for nearly two decades, including third-party capital and insurance-linked securities (ILS).

item.title: Acies MGU expands into marine insurance with launch of TEDmar International
item.description: Acies MGU (Acies), a technology and data-driven managing general underwriter (MGU) specialising in the creation and management of niche insurance businesses, has announced its expansion into the marine insurance sector through the launch of TEDmar International (TEDmar), a managing general agent dedicated to the ports and terminals market. They are leading experts in marine insurance, and we’re looking forward to supporting TEDmar’s growth as Acies expands its diverse portfolio of specialist MGAs.” The company stated that TEDmar’s international proposition is fully backed by a consortium providing Lloyd’s capacity and is designed to meet the insurance needs of port authorities and ports and terminals operators.

item.title: FurtherAI hires Zachary Hirsch as SVP of Sales
item.description: FurtherAI, an insurance AI platform, has announced the appointment of Zachary Hirsch as Senior Vice President of Sales. Hirsch joins FurtherAI after more than six years at Verkada, where he most recently served as VP of Sales, NYC + PHL + HQ Select. In his new role, Hirsch will lead the company’s commercial organisation and go-to-market strategy as FurtherAI expands its customer base across carriers, managing general agents, brokers, and wholesalers.

item.title: Swiss Re appoints Damien Bartlett and Karen Tan to L&H leadership roles
item.description: Global reinsurer Swiss Re has announced the appointments of Damien Bartlett as Head of Market Unit Life & Health UK and Ireland and Middle East and Africa, and Karen Tan as Chief Underwriting Officer for L&H Re. Bartlett joins Swiss Re following 25 years at SCOR, where he held a number of senior leadership roles. She has held several leadership roles at Swiss Re, including Head of Life & Health Products Asia and Chief Risk Officer for Asia Pacific.

item.title: Wildfire Forces Evacuations Across Top Canadian Wine Region
item.description: More than 20,000 people were ordered to evacuate one of Canada’s top wine-producing regions as an uncontrolled wildfire spread rapidly, forcing local authorities to declare a province-wide state of emergency. Authorities ordered the town of Summerland and nearby communities in British Columbia’s Okanagan Valley to be evacuated on Saturday as the Bald Range wildfire advanced. Prime Minister Mark Carney posted on social media Saturday that the federal government “stands ready to help and support the government of British Columbia in these efforts.” Last month, a blaze in the eastern Canadian province of Ontario produced smoke that darkened skies and worsened air quality as far south as Washington, DC.

item.title: Markets/Coverages: Rokstone’s Athena Cyber Division Launches Supply Chain Extension
item.description: Rokstone, the London-based specialty re/insurance managing general agent (MGA), announced that its new Athena Cyber Division has launched a customer and supplier supply chain disruption extension. Unlike traditional contingency business interruption cover, Rokstone Athena’s cyber supply chain extension responds where a cyber-attack on a key supplier prevents an insured from operating, or where an incident affecting a major customer prevents them from purchasing an insured’s goods/services. “Our new extension recognizes that cyber events disrupt not only an organization’s own systems, but also the wider commercial relationships on which they depend,” commented Debbie Hobbs, president and head of Cyber at Rokstone Athena, in a statement.

item.title: Lincoln Financial CFO to depart
item.description: Lincoln Financial announced that CFO Chris Neczypor is leaving the company to pursue an opportunity outside the insurance industry. Neczypor, who has served as CFO for the past three years, will remain with Lincoln through the end of August to support the transition. Adam Cohen, Lincoln’s chief accounting officer and treasurer, has been named interim CFO, effective immediately.

item.title: Exzeo launches AI venture division
item.description: Exzeo has launched Exzeo Ventures, a new division focused on building AI-native products, services, and businesses, primarily around insurance. The division will primarily develop initiatives internally, drawing on Exzeo’s existing insurance and technology capabilities. Rather than using AI simply to automate existing workflows, Exzeo Ventures will look for opportunities and business models that the company believes weren’t economically or technologically feasible before AI.

item.title: Allstate Introduces Large Language Model, ALLIE
item.description: Allstate CEO Tom Wilson said the insurer has a “technology-drive strategy, not a strategy supported by technology.” And the next step in the strategy is the build of ALLIE – Allstate’s Large Language Intelligent Ecosystem. The coordination and configuration of the computer systems it has already built “is helping us accelerate the build and deployment of ALLIE.” Wilson told the analysts that the large language model is “just another step along the continuum that we’ve been on for a long time” when it comes to artificial intelligence. He said Allstate spends a “tremendous amount of time and effort on cybersecurity,” adding he is “concerned about the large language models that now break out on their own and tell other agents how to do it without getting caught.”

item.description: REVO Insurance S.p.A., an Italian speciality non-life insurer, has announced the submission of a binding offer to acquire Luxembourg-based Eurocaution S.A. item.description: Taylor Farms on Sunday said it was recalling more than a dozen prepared food items containing jalapeños, including salsas and guacamole, from retailers over concerns about potential salmonella contamination. Taylor Farms is unaware of any reported illnesses linked to the voluntarily recalled items the statement added. health authorities investigate a Salmonella outbreak linked to jalapeño peppers imported from Mexico that earlier this week had sickened 345 people across 27 states and led to 36 hospitalizations.

item.title: Heat Deaths Top 25,000 in Europe as Scorching Weather Persists
item.description: Extreme heat has killed more than 25,000 people across Europe this year, according to the latest available data compiled by Bloomberg. Germany recorded the highest toll, with an estimated 11,900 excess deaths linked to heat since April, according to the Robert Koch Institute . Western Europe has been seared by four heat waves this summer, shattering temperature records and denting economic output.

item.title: OpenAI Pauses Some Work on New Astra Model on Cyber Concerns
item.description: OpenAI said it’s now taking steps to improve security controls for developing and testing newer models and “pausing internal activities involving Astra that do not yet meet these strengthened security control requirements.” Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman said the company is working to make the model “generally available.” “Given its cyber capabilities, we need a little longer to do this safely,” Altman said Friday in a social media post . OpenAI is pausing some internal work around one of its upcoming artificial intelligence models to implement stricter safeguards after the system was found to be significantly more adept at cybersecurity tasks. The ChatGPT maker said on Friday it “cannot rule out” that the unreleased Astra model would reach OpenAI’s “critical cybersecurity threshold,” meaning it’s capable of identifying and developing zero-day exploits without human intervention.

item.title: Berkshire Hathaway P&C reinsurance boosted by Tokio Marine deal, as property volumes fall
item.description: While Berkshire Hathaway has reported declining premium volumes in property business across both its primary insurance and reinsurance businesses, likely due to the softening of pricing we assume, its P&C reinsurance arm was boosted by the recent agreement and whole account deal with Tokio Marine. Berkshire Hathaway, the American multinational conglomerate holding company, reported that its recently entered into whole account quota share reinsurance agreement with Tokio Marine boosted premium volumes in the second-quarter, which otherwise would have fallen primarily due to lower property underwriting volumes. Recall that, back in the first-quarter of this year, Berkshire Hathaway’s reinsurance arm National Indemnity Company (NICO) acquired a 2.5% stake in the Japanese insurer, in a deal that comprised the following three key elements: strategic equity investment in Tokio Marine Holdings, Inc., collaboration in reinsurance, and strategic collaboration in M&A and global investment opportunities.

item.title: Gradient AI refreshes brand as business scales
item.description: Gradient AI has introduced a new brand identity as the insurance AI company looks to reflect its expansion beyond its startup roots. Founded in 2018, Gradient AI provides AI-powered decision intelligence to carriers, TPAs, brokers, self-insured employers, MGAs and other insurance organizations across group health, P&C and workers’ compensation. The company said it has experienced double-digit year-over-year growth and has built a data lake spanning tens of millions of policies and claims.

item.title: Intact launches $1 million Olympian community grant program
item.description: Intact Insurance and the Canadian Olympic Committee (COC) have launched Intact Olympian Impact, a three-year, C$1 million program that will fund community sports initiatives led by Team Canada Olympians. The initiative builds on the former OLY Canada Legacy Grant program and has previously supported projects including Charles Hamelin’s Glissez vers l’Integration , Laura Stacey’s S7 Sticks In For Charity Road Hockey Tournament , and Oluseyi Smith’s Racing to Zero . The program will award grants to Canadian Olympians to support projects focused on expanding access to sport, promoting healthy play for youth, and advancing sustainability, in line with the COC’s Team Canada 2035 strategy centered on Play, Podium, and Planet.

item.title: Inszone acquires Washington employee benefits agency Radwick & Lightle
item.description: Inszone Insurance has acquired The Lightle Group, LLC, doing business as Radwick & Lightle, expanding its employee benefits operations in Washington. The acquisition brings Radwick & Lightle’s employee benefits team into Inszone, providing access to a broader range of insurance markets, technology, and operational resources while maintaining the agency’s existing client service model. Founded in 2001 by Curt Lightle and based in Bremerton, Washington, Radwick & Lightle specializes in employee benefits for small and midsize businesses, offering benefits consulting, HR support, compliance services, and claims advocacy.

item.title: Open finance en Perú pone a prueba los límites regulatorios sobre los datos
item.description: La falta de claridad sobre la gestión de las entidades reguladoras en la gestión del consentimiento e intercambio de datos es lo que más preocupa a la industria sobre el próximo Sistema de Finanzas Abiertas (SFA) de Perú. La Superintendencia de Bancos, Seguros y AFP (SBS) ha declarado que mantiene coordinación con la Autoridad Nacional de Protección de Datos Personales (ANPDP) y otras autoridades, pero los bancos aún tienen dudas sobre cómo será la vigilancia y aplicación de sanciones en los acuerdos de datos compartidos. “No queda claro si la Autoridad Nacional de Protección de Datos tiene algún tipo de voz y voto en esto”, dijo a iupana un experto legal de un banco local.

item.title: Finsus cambia modelo de riesgo para prestar a conductores de plataformas
item.description: La garantía de un vehículo cambió la forma en que Finsus evalúa a los trabajadores de plataformas de transporte, pues la empresa asegura que ese respaldo le permitió adaptar sus modelos de riesgo y ofrecer crédito a un segmento que, sin esa estructura, seguiría siendo mucho más difícil de financiar. Los trabajadores de plataformas digitales han sido un segmento difícil de atender para la banca por la variabilidad de sus ingresos y la ausencia de esquemas laborales tradicionales. En América Latina y el Caribe, el 52% de estos trabajadores utiliza estas aplicaciones como una fuente complementaria de ingresos, según la OIT.

item.title: ClaimsBridge Adds Capital, Acquires DialysisPPO
item.description: (Image source: ClaimsBridge website.) ClaimsBridge (Arnold, Md.) has received a strategic investment from Eir Partners Capital (Miami) and acquired DialysisPPO (King of Prussia, Pa.), a cost-containment company focused on end-stage renal disease and chronic dialysis treatment. ClaimsBridge says Eir’s investment will provide capital and operational support while leaving its existing client team, processes and service model in place. “Eir’s investment gives us the ability to accelerate innovation for our clients and the payer market, and DialysisPPO is the strongest solution we’ve seen for one of healthcare’s most complex and expensive conditions.” Founded in 2006, DialysisPPO provides a patented program that allows health plans to capture Medicare savings on dialysis claims immediately, rather than waiting for the typical 30-month coordination period, according to ClaimsBridge.

item.title: Federated Acquires HDVI
item.description: (Image credit: Zetong Li/Unsplash.) High Definition Vehicle Insurance (HDVI; Greenville, S.C.) has been acquired by Federated Mutual Insurance Company (Owatonna, Minn.). HDVI will operate as a largely autonomous subsidiary of Federated Insurance, retaining its separate operations, employees and agency relationships. “Our success and progress attracted the attention of major organizations across the nation, and we are very pleased to have found a home with the established, value-driven, and well-capitalized Federated Insurance,” comments Adam Barnett, President and CEO, HDVI.

item.title: Meta Ordered to Pay $567 Million In New Mexico for Teen Mental Health Fund
item.description: A New Mexico state court ordered Meta on Thursday to pay $567 million into a teen mental health fund and change how its platforms function for young users after finding the company is to blame for harming children’s wellbeing. The ruling comes five months after a New Mexico jury in an earlier phase of the case ordered Meta to pay $375 million after finding it violated consumer protection law by misrepresenting the safety of Facebook and Instagram for young users. Biedscheid on Thursday ordered Meta to implement youth-safety measures, including monthly limits on teens’ use of Facebook and Instagram, restrictions on notifications, tighter controls on adult contact with minors, safeguards for AI chatbots, and enhanced review of child sexual abuse reports, under a decree that will be in place for five years.
